text:
alice.sre: alert — customers reporting intermittent 502/504 and timeouts to hosted inference API since 09:12 UTC :rotating_light:

bob.oncall: seeing gateway 502/504 spikes in us-west and eu-west, error rate ~6% last 15m. backlog on proxy queues

carla-runtime: quick check — there was a deploy at 09:09 that adjusted proxy connect/idle timeouts and a new autoscaler tweak rolled out at 09:08

dan-support: multiple support tickets: customers A, B, C reporting 504s on /v1/generate and embedding endpoints. screenshots attached, correlation to request size seems inconsistent

alice.sre: pulling logs now, sending samples to the channel

carla-runtime: tail from one proxy:
```
2026-03-17T09:11:34Z gateway proxy: dial tcp 10.2.5.8:8080: connection refused
2026-03-17T09:11:35Z gateway: upstream timeout after 3s
2026-03-17T09:11:36Z batcher: queue depth 420, head latency 1800ms
```

bob.oncall: looks like the short connect timeout (3s) is causing fast upstream failures and the autoscaler didn't scale quickly enough, leading to queue pileup and cascading timeouts

carla-runtime: proposed immediate mitigations: 1) revert timeout change to 10s, 2) temporarily disable new autoscaler policy, 3) open fallback routing to model-variant (lower memory) for heavy customers

emily-product: agreed — product handles comms. I'll draft status page blurb and customer notices once mitigations are applied

alice.sre: executing mitigations now. step 1: rolling timeout bump on proxies -> set connect+read=10s

deploy-bot: rollout started: config cfg-20260317-09-13 -> proxies (rolling, 5 pods at a time)

carla-runtime: step 2: disabling autoscaler annotation on inference-pool deployments (`autoscale.policy=off`) and scaling to a safe cap of 30 replicas to avoid thrash

bob.oncall: step 3: activating fallback route for top 10 customers to model-v1-quantized to reduce per-request memory and CPU pressure
dan-support: customer A reported their errors dropped to zero after fallback was applied, customer B seeing fewer 504s too

alice.sre: health metrics now: error rate dropped from 6% -> 0.9% in 12 minutes, queue depth down to ~40. latency normalizing

emily-product: posted initial status update to status.redwood.ai with note about ongoing investigation and mitigation, ETA for full recovery 30m

carla-runtime: logs show a problematic combination: aggressive autoscale downpolicy + tightened proxy timeout = upstream conns closed too aggressively. Need to revert the timeout change in the pipeline and add a pre-deploy smoke test

bob.oncall: agreed. also recommend adding a circuit breaker on the gateway so a failing pool doesn't cause cross-pool backpressure

alice.sre: immediate actions completed. next: postmortem and action items. suggested owners:
- Revert timeout change in CI pipeline -> carla-runtime
- Add gate for timeout changes (smoke test) -> carla-runtime + eng-sre
- Autoscaler simulation and safer defaults -> bob.oncall + eng-infra
- Circuit breaker implementation design -> alice.sre + eng-runtime
- Customer follow-up and SLA notes -> emily-product + dan-support

emily-product: scheduling incident review at 13:00 UTC. will invite eng-runtime, eng-sre, support, infra, and product ops

dan-support: I'll follow up with affected customers with remediation steps and a note that fallback was applied; include expected timeline for full revert

incident-bot: incident record created INC-20260317-001, severity=high, mitigation_phase=completed

alice.sre: thanks all — closing active mitigation. keep this thread for postmortem notes and assign action item tickets. :thumbsup:
